- shot from the side of gromit (impossibly) finding a winding path under the table, brows furrowed but determined

- shot of wallace at the back of the train, from the side, following the same path

- shot from under the table, facing forwards, seeing our heroes continue into the room

title: Show HN: World Watcher – a map to seamlessly watch public webcam streams
text:
World Watcher is an interactive map of live webcams around the world, that prioritizes smooth UX and correct geolocation of cameras.

The idea is to have a better experience of navigating live webcam streams that are publicly available on YouTube. There were already a few livecam aggregators out there that include a map, but I found none of them satisfying to use, as they always require you to open new pages to watch the streams. On World Watcher, you can jump from place to place seamlessly.

New streams are added to the map regurlarly. Dead streams are removed/replaced within hours. You can filter the streams by type of place or features, for example beaches or cams with audio. And if you don't know where to go, just try out the Explore button and go on a journey.

The project started getting noticed last month, and has been shared around on social media. Frank Jacobs wrote a very nice article about it on his online column Strange Maps.[1]

Have fun exploring!

The way C handles (prior to C23) booleans is pretty close to how you'd handle booleans in assembly.

CPUs don't have types, everything is integers or floats. You do your work on registers which have fixed sizes. CPUs have built in instructions for "is this register not zero" which leaks into C. 1 is true in C, but so is 2.

Also, single bits are rarely used for booleans because it requires more CPU power to extract a single bit. Everything is byte aligned at a minimum.

When doing something like network code, if you want to store a bunch of booleans you are typically going to either pack them into a byte, or you'll burn the extra bits and send a single byte for the boolean value. Typically this was flags and masks.
